title: Neutron Interferometers from Stacked Holographic Photopolymer Gratings
authors: Saba Shams-Lahijani, Tobias Jenke, Juergen Klepp, Christian Pruner, Martin Fally
abstract: Long-wavelength neutron interferometry using discrete optical elements is notoriously challenging due to stringent alignment and stability requirements. Here, we introduce a monolithic double-Laue neutron interferometer fabricated from a stack of commercial Bayfol HX photopolymer films. By recording holographic gratings simultaneously in multiple layers, we create a robust device that is inherently aligned, bypassing traditional stability problems. We demonstrate the device's function by observing the characteristic interference fringes in the diffracted intensity of both light and very cold neutrons. The interferometer is then used to perform in-situ characterization of the neutron beam's spectral profile, demonstrating its utility as a compact spectrometer. Our work establishes stacked holographic gratings as a simple, versatile, and powerful platform for matter-wave interferometry and metrology.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, stable platform for neutron interferometry by fabricating a double-Laue interferometer from stacked holographic photopolymer gratings. The technique bypasses alignment issues associated with traditional setups, allowing for the observation of neutron interference fringes. Furthermore, the device is demonstrated to function as a compact spectrometer capable of characterizing the spectral profile of the neutron beam.
main_problem: To develop a simple, versatile, and robust platform for matter-wave interferometry and metrology using neutron interferometers, overcoming traditional alignment and stability challenges.
main_result: The authors successfully fabricated a monolithic double-Laue neutron interferometer using stacked photopolymer gratings, demonstrating its function for both light and very cold neutrons.
method: They utilized holographic recording to create stacked gratings (SPSP configuration) in a single process, allowing for in-situ characterization of the neutron beam's spectral profile.
model_or_system: The physical system is a monolithic double-Laue neutron interferometer made from stacked photopolymer films. The analysis involves modeling light diffraction using a 2CW approach and neutron diffraction using a 3CW transfer-matrix approach.
key_observables: Characteristic interference fringes in diffracted intensity for both light and very cold neutrons; diffraction efficiency ($\eta_{\pm 1}(\Theta)$) as a function of angle of incidence ($\Theta$).
important_parameters: Neutron wavelength ($\lambda_N \approx 5.5$ nm); grating period ($\Lambda \approx 493$ nm); substrate separation distance ($d_S$); and the spectral distribution modeled by an Exponentially Modified Gaussian (EMG).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that higher-order harmonics are negligible for the polymer material, and that the broad neutron spectrum can be accurately modeled by an EMG distribution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the stacked grating configurations (SPPS and SPSP) and schematics of the LL-interferometer. Data show the angular dependence of diffraction efficiency for both light and neutrons, fitted to theoretical models.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the monolithic grating platform, details the fabrication and theoretical modeling (light and neutron optics), presents experimental measurements using VCNs, and concludes by demonstrating the device's utility as a compact spectrometer.
why_interesting: The work provides a highly practical, robust platform for neutron optics experiments, directly applicable to quantum sensing and metrology by simplifying complex alignment requirements inherent to traditional interferometers.
